source_text: Eadem regula ueritatis docet nos credere post patrem etiam in filium dei, Christum Iesum, dominum deum nostrum, sed dei filium; huius dei qui et unus et solus est, conditor scilicet rerum omnium, ut iam et superius expressum est. hunc enim Iesum Christum, iterum dicam huius dei filium, et in ueteri testamento legimus esse repromissum et in nouo testamento animaduertimus exhibitum, omnium sacramentorum umbras et figuras de praesentia corporatae ueritatis implentem. hunc enim Abrahae filium, hunc Dauid, non minus et uetera praedicta et euangelia testantur. ipsa Genesis, cum dicit: dabo et semini tuo; hunc quando luctatum ostendit hominem cum iacob; hunc, quando dicit: on deficiet princeps de Iuda, neque dux de Femoribus eius, donec ueniat is cui repromissum est, et ipse erit exspectatio gentium. hunc Moyses, cum dicit: prouide alium quem mittas; hunc idem, quando testatur, prophetam uobis, dicendo, suscitabit deus ex fratribus uestris: eum quasi me audite; hunc, quando dicit: videbitis uitam uestram pendentem nocte ac die, et non credetis ei. hunc Esaias: prodiet uirga de radice Iesse, et flos de radice etus ascendet; hunc eundem, quando dicit: ecce uirgo concipiet et pariet filium,; hunc, quando sanitates ab eo futuras collocat dicens: tunc aperientur oculi caecorum, et aures surdorum audient: tunc saliet claudus ut ceruus, et Diserta erit lingua mutorum; hunc, quando patientiae uirtutes expromit dicens: non audietur in plateis uox eius; harundinem quassatam non conteret, et linum fumigans non exstinguet; hunc, quando eius euangelia descripsit: e dzsponam uobis testamentum aeternum, sancta Daud fidelia; hunc, quando gentes in ipsum credituras prophetat: ecce posui eum in principium et praecipientem gentibus. gentes quae te non nouerunt inuocabunt te, et populi qui te nesciunt ad te confugient; hunc eundem, quando ad passionem eius exclamat dicens: sicut ouis ad occisionem ductus est, et sicut agnus coram tondente se sine uoce, sic non aperuit os suum in humilitate; hanc quando flagrorum eius ictus plagasque descripsit: liuore eius nos sanati sumus; aut humilitatem: et uidimus eum, et non erat ei species neque honor. homo in plaga et sciens ferre infirmitatem; aut quod populus non erat crediturus: tota die expandi manus meas ad populum non credentem; aut quod resurrecturus a mortuis: e erit in illa die radix Iesse, et qui surget imperare gentibus, in eum gentes sperabunt, et erit requies eius honor; aut cum tempus resurrectionis: quasi diluculo paratum inueniemus eum; aut quod sessurus ad dextram patris: dixit dominus domino meo: sede ad dexteram meam, donec ponam inimicos tuos scabellum pedum tuorum; aut cum possessor omnium collocatur: postula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditatem tuam, et possessionem tuam terminos terrae; aut quod iudex omnium ostenditur: deus iudicium tuum regi da, et iustitiam tuam filio regis. nec hoc in loco plura persequar, quae annuntiata de Christo omnibus haereticis sed et ipsis ueritatem tenentibus magis nota sunt.
thought_title: Belief in the Son of God
pass_a_gloss: The same rule of truth teaches us to believe after the Father also in the Son of God, Christ Jesus, our Lord God, but the Son of God; of this God who is one and only, namely the creator of all things, as has already been expressed above. For we read in the Old Testament and notice in the New Testament that this Jesus Christ, whom I will say again is the Son of this God, was promised and is shown to fulfill the shadows and figures of all sacraments with the bodily presence of truth. For Abraham and David, and not less the ancient prophecies and the Gospels, testify to this. Genesis itself, when it says: I will give to your seed; when it shows a man wrestling with Jacob; when it says: the prince will not fail from Judah, nor the leader from his thighs, until he comes to whom it has been promised, and he will be the expectation of the nations. Moses, when he says: provide another whom you will send; the same, when he testifies, saying: God will raise up a prophet from your brothers: listen to him as to me; when he says: you will see your life hanging night and day, and you will not believe him. Isaiah: a rod will come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower will ascend from his root; the same, when he says: behold, a virgin will conceive and bear a son; when he says that healings will come from him, saying: then the eyes of the blind will be opened, and the ears of the deaf will hear; then the lame will leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute will be clear; when he describes his virtues of patience, saying: his voice will not be heard in the streets; he will not break a bruised reed, and he will not extinguish a smoking flax; when he describes his Gospel: behold, I will make a covenant with you, the faithful holy ones of David; when he prophesies that the nations will believe in him: behold, I have set him as a witness to the nations, the nations that do not know you will call upon you, and the peoples that do not know you will flee to you; the same, when he exclaims about his passion, saying: he was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb before his shearer, he did not open his mouth in humility; when he describes the blows and wounds of his scourging: by his stripes we are healed; or his humility: and we saw him, and he had no form or honor, a man in a plague and knowing how to bear infirmity; or that the people would not believe: I have stretched out my hands all day to a people that does not believe; or that he will rise from the dead: he will be the root of Jesse, and he who will rise to rule the nations, in him the nations will hope, and his rest will be honor; or when the time of resurrection: we will find him like the dawn; or that he will sit at the right hand of the Father: the Lord said to my Lord: sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet; or when he is given possession of all things: ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession; or that he is shown as the judge of all: God, give your judgment to the king, and your justice to the son of the king. Nor will I pursue more things in this place, which have been announced about Christ, and are more known to all heretics and to those who hold the truth.

pass_b_english: The same rule of truth teaches us to believe, after the Father, also in the Son of God, Christ Jesus, our Lord God, but the Son of God — of this God who is one and only, namely the Creator of all things, as has already been expressed above.

For in the Old Testament we read, and in the New Testament we see fulfilled, that this Jesus Christ — I say again, the Son of this God — was promised and is shown to fill the shadows and figures of all the sacraments with the bodily presence of truth.
Abraham and David testify to this, and no less do the ancient prophecies and the Gospels.

Genesis itself, when it says, "I will give to your seed" (Genesis); when it shows a man wrestling with Jacob (Genesis); when it says, "The prince shall not fail from Judah, nor the ruler from his thighs, until he comes to whom it has been promised, and he shall be the expectation of the nations" (Genesis).

Moses, when he says, "Provide another whom you will send" (Genesis); the same Moses, when he testifies, saying, "God will raise up a prophet from among your brothers: listen to him as you would me" (Deuteronomy); when he says, "You will see your life hanging in doubt night and day, and you will not believe him" (Deuteronomy).

Isaiah: "A rod shall come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise from his root" (Isaiah); the same prophet, when he says, "Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son" (Isaiah); when he declares that healings will come from him, saying, "Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall hear; then the lame shall leap like a deer, and the tongue of the mute shall be clear" (Isaiah); when he proclaims his virtues of patience, saying, "His voice shall not be heard in the streets; a bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not extinguish" (Isaiah); when he describes his Gospel: "Behold, I will make an everlasting covenant with you, the faithful mercies of David" (Isaiah); when he prophesies that the nations will believe in him: "Behold, I have made him a witness to the peoples, a leader and commander for the peoples. Nations that did not know you shall run to you, and peoples that did not know you shall flee to you" (Isaiah); the same prophet, when he cries out concerning his passion: "He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and like a lamb before its shearer is silent, so he did not open his mouth in humility" (Isaiah); when he describes the blows and wounds of his scourging: "By his stripes we are healed" (Isaiah); or his humility: "And we saw him, and he had no form or comeliness; a man of sorrows and acquainted with infirmity" (Isaiah); or that the people would not believe: "I have stretched out my hands all day to a people that does not believe" (Isaiah); or that he will rise from the dead: "In that day the root of Jesse shall stand as a signal to the peoples; him shall the nations seek, and his rest shall be glorious" (Isaiah); or concerning the time of resurrection: "We shall find him ready like the dawn" (Isaiah); or that he will sit at the right hand of the Father: "The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool" (Psalm); or when he is given possession of all things: "Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance, and the ends of the earth as your possession" (Psalm); or that he is shown as the judge of all: "Give the king your judgment, O God, and your justice to the king's son" (Psalm).
Nor will I pursue further matters in this place, which have been announced concerning Christ and are more known to all heretics and to those who hold the truth.
